source.title: Task-Specific Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Monosemantic Neuronal Activations
source.authors: Da Ma; Gonghu Shang; Zhi Chen; Li-Bo Qin; Yijie Luo; Hong-Shen Xu; Lei Pan; Shuai Fan; Kai Yu; Lu Chen

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures activation overlap across language-model inputs using a visualization rather than the original neuron-level interpretability method. It also compares raw polysemantic activations with SAE representations, but its data-selection performance results alone do not test the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The direct claim-relevant result is the qualitative visualization of raw activations for Math and Code examples (Figure 4). The SAE-versus-polysemantic downstream data-selection results are recorded under fits_no_version: they compare selection outcomes, not the prevalence or semantic meaning of polysemantic neurons. Other data-selection benchmarks and method ablations do not measure the claim’s object.
record.test_reason: This is a data-selection method paper (MoNA). Polysemanticity is cited from Bricken et al. as motivation, not measured. The only neuron-level evidence is Figure 4, a qualitative plot of sample-level TopK gated-MLP activations over 100 Math and 100 Code samples on the top-100 most variant neurons. Overlap of token-averaged activations between two task sets does not show that individual neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts. The paper gives no share of neurons, no per-neuron semantics and no layer comparison. Math and Code are also not clearly unrelated. Every other result is downstream performance of the authors' own selection method.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors propose MoNA and conclude that SAE-derived monosemantic activations give more semantically aligned, interpretable and better task-specific data selection than baselines. Polysemanticity of raw neurons is assumed from prior work as the reason raw activations create spurious similarity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layer activations and SAE-derived sparse features to select instruction-tuning data; it does not reproduce the original neuron visualization or feature-inspection procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: For data-selection performance, the paper reports that deeper layers, especially the penultimate layer, perform strongly; very small K reduces performance, while gains diminish as K increases; Jaccard outperforms Cosine and Euclidean in the reported comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: For LLaMA3-8B, TopK raw gated-MLP activations on the 100 most variant neurons overlap heavily between Math and Code samples, while SAE features separate the tasks (qualitative, Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-level (token-averaged) raw MLP activation patterns in LLMs overlap across distinct tasks more than SAE feature patterns do.

fits_no_version.finding: Data selection using SAE features beats raw gated-MLP activations and raw hidden states on MMLU, BBH, TydiQA and their average (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this data-selection setup, SAE-derived representations give better instruction-tuning data selection than raw neuron activations.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released but gives no URL
record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (listed venue); the paper text also identifies the document as a preprint under review
record.problems: The claim-relevant visualization is qualitative and restricted to the top-100 most variant neurons and two task sample sets; it gives no numerical share of neurons or per-neuron semantic explanations. The Table 8 backbone is not identified in that table, and uncertainty estimates are not reported there.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. Other data-selection and tuning ablations were not included because they do not measure neuron polysemanticity or the activation-overlap behavior.

untested.parts: No share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, no per-neuron inspection, no layer comparison.
Causes of polysemanticity under sufficient capacity not tested.
No variation of architecture, activation function or regularization affecting polysemanticity.
No analysis of whether mixed neurons detect a shared feature.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with a V2 'supports' label is downgraded. Figure 4 is an illustrative plot for the method, not a measurement of how common polysemantic neurons are. Table 8's 'w/o SAE' row duplicates the DLRDS-LLaMA3-8B baseline numbers from Table 1. The polysemantic representation uses TopK (K=192) on |SiLU(W_gate x)| from the same layer as the SAE.

versions.untested_parts: No vision model or image-classifier neuron is studied.

The paper reports qualitative overlap for selected high-variance neurons on Math and Code examples, but does not estimate the share of all MLP neurons, compare layers for polysemanticity, or test unrelated tokens or contexts beyond these task samples.
No test of superposition or of whether feature count exceeds neuron count.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity under sufficient capacity.

The paper varies SAE settings for data selection but does not measure how architecture, activation function, or regularization changes the share of polysemantic neurons, or whether that share can be lowered without substantial performance loss.
The paper does not investigate whether individual mixed-activation neurons detect a shared feature or related offshoots of one job.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for deciding whether neurons are polysemantic.

rows.subject: LLaMA3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Visualized raw gated-MLP neuron activation profiles across Math and Code samples.
rows.baseline: SAE monosemantic profiles are described as having clear task-specific patterns
rows.value: The paper describes substantial activation overlap: many neurons, especially those with high activation peaks, are activated by both tasks.
rows.note: This is a qualitative result for the selected neurons and task samples, not an estimate of the proportion of all MLP neurons.
rows.check: Measures cross-task overlap of token-averaged, TopK-sparsified (K=192) |SiLU(W_gate x)| activations, apparently from the penultimate layer of LLaMA3-8B (Appendix B.3 says same layer and K as the SAE). This does not show single neurons responding to unrelated concepts, and gives no share of neurons. It is illustrative support for the method, so it is not evidence on V2.
